recipes.name: Pistachio Cake
ingredients_raw: 1 (3.4 ounce) package instant pistachio pudding mix

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 10-inch Bundt or tube pan.
Process pistachios in a food processor until nuts become smooth and creamy, 7 to 10 minutes, stopping to scrape down sides of bowl as needed. Set aside.
Whisk cake mix and pudding mix together in a large bowl, create a well in the center.
Add water, eggs, oil, processed pistachios, green food coloring, and pistachio extract into center of well. Whisk together until fully combined.
Bake in the preheated oven until cake springs back when lightly pressed, or a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean, 50 to 55 minutes.
Cool in the pan for 15 minutes. Turn out onto a wire rack and cool completely.
To make the glaze: Whisk together powdered sugar, heavy cream, and vanilla extract in a small bowl until fully combined.
Spoon glaze evenly over cooled cake, garnish with chopped pistachios, slice and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Pistachio Cake
raw_recipe.description: This moist pistachio cake made with real pistachio butter, cake mix, and pistachio pudding is topped with a sweet glaze for a delightful dessert.

review.reviewBody: I love this cake and make it often. Everyone at work loves it too. I frost it will a 16 oz container of Cool Whip mixed with a box of instant pistachio pudding and it is very moist and fabulous! I bake it in a bundt pan and it comes out perfect everytime.
Never add pudding to a cake mix that already has pudding in it. That's what makes it fail. Always start with a cake mix with NO pudding in the mix. Duncan Hines. Works every time.

After I spray cooking spray in my Bundt pan, I coat the pan with a cinnamon sugar mixture and shake out the excess. I also put a glaze on the top instead of the powdered sugar. I use powdered sugar, milk or water and a few drops of orange flavor. Before the glaze dries, I sprinkle chopped pistachio nuts on the top. Fabulous!

I’ve been making this recipe now for several months and it always seems to be a winner in the flavor department. I had the same issue as everyone else with the cake falling and turning out with a bit of a gluey texture. So, I asked a baking friend for suggestions. Now, whenever I make this, I separate all the egg yolks from the whites and mix the yolks in with the rest of the recipe as described. Then, I whip up the whites separately to medium peaks and then gently fold them into the batter just before pouring the batter into my prepared pan(s). The other trick that helps is baking the cake for the full time, or longer if needed. Both of these have helped with the falling and improved the texture. So far, the most successful combination has been Devils Food cake mix with Coconut Creme pudding mix. I’ve also added a bit of instant coffee powder to the dry mix and coconut extract for the coconut flavoring to boost both flavors. Mix in some mini chocolate chips and it’s a huge hit!

After many tries I have finally found the remedy for the rise and fall of this recipe! 

1 pkg of Duncan Hines yellow cake mix (it's the only one without pudding in the mix! That's crucial!)
1 small pkg of pistachio pudding mix
1/2 cup of sugar
4 eggs
1/2 cup of water
1/2 cup of vegetable oil
1 8 oz. Cup of sour cream
1/2 tsp of almond extract
Several drops of green food coloring

Mix all ingredients together and pour into greased and floured bundt pan (or the spray with the flour in it)
Bake at 350 for 1:05 to 1:10. 
Came out perfectly! !!!! A huge HIT with the family!

I made this cake for St. Patrick’s Day. It was a huge hit with the family. I didn’t have a tube pan, so I used two round cake pans and the recipe worked out well with them. Like a previous baker, I mixed two tubs of cool whip with instant pistachio pudding as well and iced the cake with that. It was the perfect addition to an already delicious and moist cake. It made it taste so light and fluffy. I even froze some of this cake and my dad enjoyed it later. He said that he’ll make a special request for this cake for his birthday later this year!

Delicious, moist and easy! It was a super-hit when I served it at a party. The only changes I made were that I swapped milk for water, and added a few large handfuls of chopped pistachios into the batter. I also beat my eggs first, then added the other ingredients. After cooling completely, I frosted the cake with a simple lemon buttercream and added more chopped pistachios on top. The only downside is that pistachios are so darn expensive!

Added 1/3 cup of chopped pistachios on top and mixed 1/3 cup within the cake. Did not add water because I mixed the pistachio pudding with half and half (almost per the box instructions). Made the cake very moist, will add a dollop of whipped cream when serving.

additional touches -->I add 1/3 cup of sour cream and also a sugar walnut mixture of cinnamon / white and brown sugars and crushed walnuts in the center and atop the bundt batter so its flavored at the bottom when you turn it over.

I love this recipe, but I beat it for 5 minutes on high instead of 3 minutes and find the cake keeps its shape every time! Never had a problem with it collapsing. I am going to switch out the pistachio with a cherry pudding, and add Cool Whip and cherry pie filling for a topping, for a Valentine's pot luck lunch at work.

Rave reviews at St. Patrick's party. I did add 1/4 cup crushed pistachio nuts to batter. I used the pudding and cool whip on top with another 1/4 cup of the nuts. I had no problems with bunt cake falling. Just as tasty as it looked.

I was a little hesitant about making the pistachio butter but it went fine. I did not need the stated 7-10 minutes in my food processor. I kept checking and it probably took maybe 5 minutes at the most to get to a smooth and creamy consistency. It was like soft Playdo and I wondered how well it would mix with the other ingredients. Instead of whisking, I used an electric mixer and everything blended together beautifully. It turned out moist and flavorful and quite lovely with the glaze and chopped pistachios sprinkled on top. I took my cake to an office potluck and it was a hit—people requested the recipe.
For my frosting, I used a packet of pistachio pudding mix, and whipped it into cool whip with a little heavy cream. So good!

I have the ingredient list for the old recipe, but not the instructions. As follows, 1 (15.25 ounce) package yellow cake mix, 1 (3.4 ounce) package instant pistachio pudding mix, 1 1/2 cups water, 4 large eggs, 1/4 cup vegetable oil, 1/2 teaspoon almond extract, 7 drops green food coloring

I saved this recipe years ago. It was a family favourite that I have often made. I noticed the the recipe was significantly changed. Even my changed my saved version. I made it anyway and no one ate it. Awful to think that this could happen to any of my cherished saved recipes! No longer will trust allrecipes. Looks beautiful just as always but it sure isn’t the perfect tasting recipe I counted on. What a waste ofingredients.
I have been making this recipe for years and when I logged in tonight, I found it had significantly changed. I would like the old recipe back. This cake should be a separate post.
This is identical to my husband's grandmother's cake recipe that she made for every birthday. We skip the food dye-- the cake is plenty green! We add a bittersweet chocolate frosting and it's HEAVEN.
